text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Turkey expects the right and left to unite after public pressure brought the end of the Islamist-led government.
- Control of the economy is passed on to Gunes Taner and Isin Celebi of the right-wing Motherland Party, who shared responsibility for economic affairs in the 1987-1991 period.
- The leader of a key left-wing party which has pledged to support the new secularist coalition is to give the government a six-month period of grace.
- Turkey's $4 billion project for 145 new attack helicopters begins with the invitation to companies to make bids.
- The unarmed forces start to work. The Islamist-led government, which caused tension in the armed forces, has been wiped away from the political stage by the new coalition.
- The business community expects Turkey's 55th government to introduce economic reforms.
- The tourism sector has brought new proposals for casinos to save them from closure by introducing expensive membership fees.
- The husband of former deputy prime minister Tansu Ciller faces the possibility of questionning over a security scandal now that she is out of office.
- The former Islamist-led government's pledge to reform the tax system was unfulfilled during its time in office.
- Tight security measures have been taken in the central Anatolian town of Sivas ahead of the fourth anniversary on July 2 of a fire in which 37 intellectuals died.
- The conservative allies of the Islamists say the new secularist government will have a life of just three months.
